name: A-pop
editorial_article: African pop—or A-pop—is a genre-fusing framework defined by South African singer Tyla in her 2026 studio album of the same name. Aiming to reclaim the pop label, Tyla described the intent as tailoring pop music to her own African heritage rather than the reverse. The sound is heavily percussive and centers on rhythms derived from amapiano, while folding in elements of R&B, dance, and electropop. On the album, Tyla collaborates with various regional artists and producers to create a globalized iteration of the style, including features from Liquideep, MaWhoo, and Babalwa M, who contributes Xhosa vocals to the track I Don't Care. Tyla has explicitly stated that African music is, by definition, pop music, seeking to dissolve the perceived separation between local African traditions and global pop culture.
editorial_definition: A-pop is an African-centered evolution of pop music that integrates percussive amapiano rhythms with global R&B and dance influences.
sonic_markers: Percussive amapiano foundations, melodic pop hooks, R&B-inflected vocals, dance-pop production.
